lambda.GetCodeSigningConfig.doc: Returns information about the specified code signing configuration.

CodeSigningConfigId.doc: Unique identifer for the Code signing configuration.

CodeSigningConfigArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Code signing configuration.

SigningProfileVersionArns.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for each of the signing profiles. A signing profile defines a trusted user who can sign a code package.

CodeSigningPolicies.doc: The code signing policy controls the validation failure action for signature mismatch or expiry.

UntrustedArtifactOnDeployment.doc: Code signing configuration policy for deployment validation failure. If you set the policy to Enforce , Lambda blocks the deployment request if signature validation checks fail. If you set the policy to Warn , Lambda allows the deployment and creates a CloudWatch log. Default value: Warn

LastModified.doc: The date and time that the Code signing configuration was last modified, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD).

lambda.GetFunction.doc: Returns information about the function or function version, with a link to download the deployment package that's valid for 10 minutes. If you specify a function version, only details that are specific to that version are returned.

Configuration.doc: The configuration of the function or version.

Runtime.doc: The identifier of the function's runtime . Runtime is required if the deployment package is a .zip file archive. Specifying a runtime results in an error if you're deploying a function using a container image. The following list includes deprecated runtimes. Lambda blocks creating new functions and updating existing functions shortly after each runtime is deprecated. For more information, see Runtime use after deprecation . For a list of all currently supported runtimes, see Supported runtimes .

Handler.doc: The function that Lambda calls to begin running your function.

CodeSize.doc: The size of the function's deployment package, in bytes.

Timeout.doc: The amount of time in seconds that Lambda allows a function to run before stopping it.

MemorySize.doc: The amount of memory available to the function at runtime.

LastModified.doc: The date and time that the function was last updated, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD).

CodeSha256.doc: The SHA256 hash of the function's deployment package.

Version.doc: The version of the Lambda function.

SubnetIds.doc: A list of VPC subnet IDs.

SecurityGroupIds.doc: A list of VPC security group IDs.

Ipv6AllowedForDualStack.doc: Allows outbound IPv6 traffic on VPC functions that are connected to dual-stack subnets.

TargetArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Amazon SQS queue or Amazon SNS topic.

Environment.doc: The function's environment variables . Omitted from CloudTrail logs.

Variables.doc: Environment variable key-value pairs. Omitted from CloudTrail logs.

Error.doc: Error messages for environment variables that couldn't be applied.

KMSKeyArn.doc: The ARN of the Key Management Service (KMS) customer managed key that's used to encrypt the following resources: The function's environment variables . The function's Lambda SnapStart snapshots. When used with SourceKMSKeyArn , the unzipped version of the .zip deployment package that's used for function invocations. For more information, see Specifying a customer managed key for Lambda . The optimized version of the container image that's used for function invocations. Note that this is not the…

MasterArn.doc: For Lambda@Edge functions, the ARN of the main function.

RevisionId.doc: The latest updated revision of the function or alias.

Arn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the function layer.

CodeSize.doc: The size of the layer archive in bytes.

SigningProfileVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for a signing profile version.

SigningJobArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a signing job.

State.doc: The current state of the function. When the state is Inactive , you can reactivate the function by invoking it.

StateReason.doc: The reason for the function's current state.

StateReasonCode.doc: The reason code for the function's current state. When the code is Creating , you can't invoke or modify the function.

LastUpdateStatus.doc: The status of the last update that was performed on the function. This is first set to Successful after function creation completes.

LastUpdateStatusReason.doc: The reason for the last update that was performed on the function.

LastUpdateStatusReasonCode.doc: The reason code for the last update that was performed on the function.

FileSystemConfigs.doc: Connection settings for an Amazon EFS file system .

item.doc: Details about the connection between a Lambda function and an Amazon EFS file system .

Arn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon EFS access point that provides access to the file system.

LocalMountPath.doc: The path where the function can access the file system, starting with /mnt/ .

PackageType.doc: The type of deployment package. Set to Image for container image and set Zip for .zip file archive.

ImageConfig.doc: Configuration values that override the container image Dockerfile.

EntryPoint.doc: Specifies the entry point to their application, which is typically the location of the runtime executable.

Command.doc: Specifies parameters that you want to pass in with ENTRYPOINT.

SigningProfileVersionArn.doc: The ARN of the signing profile version.

SigningJobArn.doc: The ARN of the signing job.

Architectures.doc: The instruction set architecture that the function supports. Architecture is a string array with one of the valid values. The default architecture value is x86_64 .

EphemeralStorage.doc: The size of the function's /tmp directory in MB. The default value is 512, but can be any whole number between 512 and 10,240 MB. For more information, see Configuring ephemeral storage (console) .

Size.doc: The size of the function's /tmp directory.

SnapStart.doc: Set ApplyOn to PublishedVersions to create a snapshot of the initialized execution environment when you publish a function version. For more information, see Improving startup performance with Lambda SnapStart .

ApplyOn.doc: When set to PublishedVersions , Lambda creates a snapshot of the execution environment when you publish a function version.

OptimizationStatus.doc: When you provide a qualified Amazon Resource Name (ARN) , this response element indicates whether SnapStart is activated for the specified function version.

RuntimeVersionConfig.doc: The ARN of the runtime and any errors that occured.

RuntimeVersionArn.doc: The ARN of the runtime version you want the function to use.

Error.doc: Error response when Lambda is unable to retrieve the runtime version for a function.

LoggingConfig.doc: The function's Amazon CloudWatch Logs configuration settings.

LogFormat.doc: The format in which Lambda sends your function's application and system logs to CloudWatch. Select between plain text and structured JSON.

ApplicationLogLevel.doc: Set this property to filter the application logs for your function that Lambda sends to CloudWatch. Lambda only sends application logs at the selected level of detail and lower, where TRACE is the highest level and FATAL is the lowest.

SystemLogLevel.doc: Set this property to filter the system logs for your function that Lambda sends to CloudWatch. Lambda only sends system logs at the selected level of detail and lower, where DEBUG is the highest level and WARN is the lowest.

LogGroup.doc: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch log group the function sends logs to. By default, Lambda functions send logs to a default log group named /aws/lambda/<function name> . To use a different log group, enter an existing log group or enter a new log group name.

Code.doc: The deployment package of the function or version.

RepositoryType.doc: The service that's hosting the file.

Location.doc: A presigned URL that you can use to download the deployment package.

ImageUri.doc: URI of a container image in the Amazon ECR registry.

ResolvedImageUri.doc: The resolved URI for the image.

SourceKMSKeyArn.doc: The ARN of the Key Management Service (KMS) customer managed key that's used to encrypt your function's .zip deployment package. If you don't provide a customer managed key, Lambda uses an Amazon Web Services owned key .

Tags.doc: The function's tags . Lambda returns tag data only if you have explicit allow permissions for lambda:ListTags .

TagsError.doc: An object that contains details about an error related to retrieving tags.

ReservedConcurrentExecutions.doc: The number of concurrent executions that are reserved for this function. For more information, see Managing Lambda reserved concurrency .

lambda.GetFunctionCodeSigningConfig.doc: Returns the code signing configuration for the specified function.

CodeSigningConfigArn.doc: The The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the code signing configuration.

FunctionName.doc: The name or ARN of the Lambda function. Name formats Function name - MyFunction . Function ARN - arn:aws:lambda:us-west-2:123456789012:function:MyFunction . Partial ARN - 123456789012:function:MyFunction . The length constraint applies only to the full ARN. If you specify only the function name, it is limited to 64 characters in length.

lambda.GetFunctionConfiguration.doc: Returns the version-specific settings of a Lambda function or version. The output includes only options that can vary between versions of a function. To modify these settings, use UpdateFunctionConfiguration . To get all of a function's details, including function-level settings, use GetFunction .

lambda.GetFunctionUrlConfig.doc: Returns details about a Lambda function URL.

FunctionUrl.doc: The HTTP URL endpoint for your function.

FunctionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of your function.

AuthType.doc: The type of authentication that your function URL uses. Set to AWS_IAM if you want to restrict access to authenticated users only. Set to NONE if you want to bypass IAM authentication to create a public endpoint. For more information, see Security and auth model for Lambda function URLs .

Cors.doc: The cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) settings for your function URL.

AllowCredentials.doc: Whether to allow cookies or other credentials in requests to your function URL. The default is false .

AllowHeaders.doc: The HTTP headers that origins can include in requests to your function URL. For example: Date , Keep-Alive , X-Custom-Header .

AllowMethods.doc: The HTTP methods that are allowed when calling your function URL. For example: GET , POST , DELETE , or the wildcard character ( * ).

AllowOrigins.doc: The origins that can access your function URL. You can list any number of specific origins, separated by a comma. For example: https://www.example.com , http://localhost:60905 . Alternatively, you can grant access to all origins using the wildcard character ( * ).

ExposeHeaders.doc: The HTTP headers in your function response that you want to expose to origins that call your function URL. For example: Date , Keep-Alive , X-Custom-Header .

MaxAge.doc: The maximum amount of time, in seconds, that web browsers can cache results of a preflight request. By default, this is set to 0 , which means that the browser doesn't cache results.

CreationTime.doc: When the function URL was created, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD).

LastModifiedTime.doc: When the function URL configuration was last updated, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD).

InvokeMode.doc: Use one of the following options: BUFFERED – This is the default option. Lambda invokes your function using the Invoke API operation. Invocation results are available when the payload is complete. The maximum payload size is 6 MB. RESPONSE_STREAM – Your function streams payload results as they become available. Lambda invokes your function using the InvokeWithResponseStream API operation. The maximum response payload size is 20 MB, however, you can request a quota increase .

lambda.GetLayerVersion.doc: Returns information about a version of an Lambda layer , with a link to download the layer archive that's valid for 10 minutes.

Location.doc: A link to the layer archive in Amazon S3 that is valid for 10 minutes.

CodeSha256.doc: The SHA-256 hash of the layer archive.

CodeSize.doc: The size of the layer archive in bytes.

SigningProfileVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for a signing profile version.

SigningJobArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a signing job.

LayerVersionArn.doc: The ARN of the layer version.

CreatedDate.doc: The date that the layer version was created, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD).

CompatibleRuntimes.doc: The layer's compatible runtimes. The following list includes deprecated runtimes. For more information, see Runtime use after deprecation . For a list of all currently supported runtimes, see Supported runtimes .

CompatibleArchitectures.doc: A list of compatible instruction set architectures .

lambda.GetPolicy.doc: Returns the resource-based IAM policy for a function, version, or alias.

RevisionId.doc: A unique identifier for the current revision of the policy.

lambda.ListEventSourceMappings.doc: Lists event source mappings. Specify an EventSourceArn to show only event source mappings for a single event source.

NextMarker.doc: A pagination token that's returned when the response doesn't contain all event source mappings.

EventSourceMappings.doc: A list of event source mappings.

item.doc: A mapping between an Amazon Web Services resource and a Lambda function. For details, see CreateEventSourceMapping .

UUID.doc: The identifier of the event source mapping.

StartingPosition.doc: The position in a stream from which to start reading. Required for Amazon Kinesis and Amazon DynamoDB Stream event sources. AT_TIMESTAMP is supported only for Amazon Kinesis streams, Amazon DocumentDB, Amazon MSK, and self-managed Apache Kafka.

StartingPositionTimestamp.doc: With StartingPosition set to AT_TIMESTAMP , the time from which to start reading. StartingPositionTimestamp cannot be in the future.

BatchSize.doc: The maximum number of records in each batch that Lambda pulls from your stream or queue and sends to your function. Lambda passes all of the records in the batch to the function in a single call, up to the payload limit for synchronous invocation (6 MB). Default value: Varies by service. For Amazon SQS, the default is 10. For all other services, the default is 100. Related setting: When you set BatchSize to a value greater than 10, you must set MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds to at least 1.

MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds.doc: The maximum amount of time, in seconds, that Lambda spends gathering records before invoking the function. You can configure MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds to any value from 0 seconds to 300 seconds in increments of seconds. For streams and Amazon SQS event sources, the default batching window is 0 seconds. For Amazon MSK, Self-managed Apache Kafka, Amazon MQ, and DocumentDB event sources, the default batching window is 500 ms. Note that because you can only change MaximumBatchingWindowInSecond…

ParallelizationFactor.doc: (Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams only) The number of batches to process concurrently from each shard. The default value is 1.

EventSourceArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the event source.

FilterCriteria.doc: An object that defines the filter criteria that determine whether Lambda should process an event. For more information, see Lambda event filtering . If filter criteria is encrypted, this field shows up as null in the response of ListEventSourceMapping API calls. You can view this field in plaintext in the response of GetEventSourceMapping and DeleteEventSourceMapping calls if you have kms:Decrypt permissions for the correct KMS key.

item.doc: A structure within a FilterCriteria object that defines an event filtering pattern.

Pattern.doc: A filter pattern. For more information on the syntax of a filter pattern, see Filter rule syntax .

FunctionArn.doc: The ARN of the Lambda function.

LastModified.doc: The date that the event source mapping was last updated or that its state changed.

LastProcessingResult.doc: The result of the last Lambda invocation of your function.

State.doc: The state of the event source mapping. It can be one of the following: Creating , Enabling , Enabled , Disabling , Disabled , Updating , or Deleting .

StateTransitionReason.doc: Indicates whether a user or Lambda made the last change to the event source mapping.

DestinationConfig.doc: (Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, Amazon MSK, and self-managed Apache Kafka event sources only) A configuration object that specifies the destination of an event after Lambda processes it.

OnSuccess.doc: The destination configuration for successful invocations.

Destination.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the destination resource.

OnFailure.doc: The destination configuration for failed invocations.

Destination.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the destination resource. To retain records of unsuccessful asynchronous invocations , you can configure an Amazon SNS topic, Amazon SQS queue, Amazon S3 bucket, Lambda function, or Amazon EventBridge event bus as the destination. To retain records of failed invocations from Kinesis , DynamoDB , self-managed Kafka or Amazon MSK , you can configure an Amazon SNS topic, Amazon SQS queue, or Amazon S3 bucket as the destination.

Topics.doc: The name of the Kafka topic.

Queues.doc: (Amazon MQ) The name of the Amazon MQ broker destination queue to consume.

SourceAccessConfigurations.doc: An array of the authentication protocol, VPC components, or virtual host to secure and define your event source.

item.doc: To secure and define access to your event source, you can specify the authentication protocol, VPC components, or virtual host.

Type.doc: The type of authentication protocol, VPC components, or virtual host for your event source. For example: "Type":"SASL_SCRAM_512_AUTH" . BASIC_AUTH – (Amazon MQ) The Secrets Manager secret that stores your broker credentials. BASIC_AUTH – (Self-managed Apache Kafka) The Secrets Manager ARN of your secret key used for SASL/PLAIN authentication of your Apache Kafka brokers. VPC_SUBNET – (Self-managed Apache Kafka) The subnets associated with your VPC. Lambda connects to these subnets to fetch data…

URI.doc: The value for your chosen configuration in Type . For example: "URI": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:01234567890:secret:MyBrokerSecretName" .

SelfManagedEventSource.doc: The self-managed Apache Kafka cluster for your event source.

Endpoints.doc: The list of bootstrap servers for your Kafka brokers in the following format: "KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS": ["abc.xyz.com:xxxx","abc2.xyz.com:xxxx"] .

MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds.doc: (Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams only) Discard records older than the specified age. The default value is -1, which sets the maximum age to infinite. When the value is set to infinite, Lambda never discards old records. The minimum valid value for maximum record age is 60s. Although values less than 60 and greater than -1 fall within the parameter's absolute range, they are not allowed

BisectBatchOnFunctionError.doc: (Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams only) If the function returns an error, split the batch in two and retry. The default value is false.

MaximumRetryAttempts.doc: (Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams only) Discard records after the specified number of retries. The default value is -1, which sets the maximum number of retries to infinite. When MaximumRetryAttempts is infinite, Lambda retries failed records until the record expires in the event source.

TumblingWindowInSeconds.doc: (Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams only) The duration in seconds of a processing window for DynamoDB and Kinesis Streams event sources. A value of 0 seconds indicates no tumbling window.

FunctionResponseTypes.doc: (Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, and Amazon SQS) A list of current response type enums applied to the event source mapping.

AmazonManagedKafkaEventSourceConfig.doc: Specific configuration settings for an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) event source.

ConsumerGroupId.doc: The identifier for the Kafka consumer group to join. The consumer group ID must be unique among all your Kafka event sources. After creating a Kafka event source mapping with the consumer group ID specified, you cannot update this value. For more information, see Customizable consumer group ID .

SelfManagedKafkaEventSourceConfig.doc: Specific configuration settings for a self-managed Apache Kafka event source.

ConsumerGroupId.doc: The identifier for the Kafka consumer group to join. The consumer group ID must be unique among all your Kafka event sources. After creating a Kafka event source mapping with the consumer group ID specified, you cannot update this value. For more information, see Customizable consumer group ID .

ScalingConfig.doc: (Amazon SQS only) The scaling configuration for the event source. For more information, see Configuring maximum concurrency for Amazon SQS event sources .

MaximumConcurrency.doc: Limits the number of concurrent instances that the Amazon SQS event source can invoke.

DocumentDBEventSourceConfig.doc: Specific configuration settings for a DocumentDB event source.

DatabaseName.doc: The name of the database to consume within the DocumentDB cluster.

CollectionName.doc: The name of the collection to consume within the database. If you do not specify a collection, Lambda consumes all collections.

FullDocument.doc: Determines what DocumentDB sends to your event stream during document update operations. If set to UpdateLookup, DocumentDB sends a delta describing the changes, along with a copy of the entire document. Otherwise, DocumentDB sends only a partial document that contains the changes.

KMSKeyArn.doc: The ARN of the Key Management Service (KMS) customer managed key that Lambda uses to encrypt your function's filter criteria .

FilterCriteriaError.doc: An object that contains details about an error related to filter criteria encryption.

ErrorCode.doc: The KMS exception that resulted from filter criteria encryption or decryption.

EventSourceMappingArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the event source mapping.

MetricsConfig.doc: The metrics configuration for your event source. For more information, see Event source mapping metrics .

Metrics.doc: The metrics you want your event source mapping to produce. Include EventCount to receive event source mapping metrics related to the number of events processed by your event source mapping. For more information about these metrics, see Event source mapping metrics .

ProvisionedPollerConfig.doc: (Amazon MSK and self-managed Apache Kafka only) The Provisioned Mode configuration for the event source. For more information, see Provisioned Mode .

MinimumPollers.doc: The minimum number of event pollers this event source can scale down to.

MaximumPollers.doc: The maximum number of event pollers this event source can scale up to.

To get the additional fields (State, StateReasonCode, StateReason, LastUpdateStatus, LastUpdateStatusReason, LastUpdateStatusReasonCode, RuntimeVersionConfig) for a function or version, use GetFunction .

PackageType.doc: The type of deployment package. Set to Image for container image and set Zip for .zip file archive.

ImageConfig.doc: Configuration values that override the container image Dockerfile.

EntryPoint.doc: Specifies the entry point to their application, which is typically the location of the runtime executable.

Command.doc: Specifies parameters that you want to pass in with ENTRYPOINT.

SigningProfileVersionArn.doc: The ARN of the signing profile version.

SigningJobArn.doc: The ARN of the signing job.

Architectures.doc: The instruction set architecture that the function supports. Architecture is a string array with one of the valid values. The default architecture value is x86_64 .

EphemeralStorage.doc: The size of the function's /tmp directory in MB. The default value is 512, but can be any whole number between 512 and 10,240 MB. For more information, see Configuring ephemeral storage (console) .

Size.doc: The size of the function's /tmp directory.

SnapStart.doc: Set ApplyOn to PublishedVersions to create a snapshot of the initialized execution environment when you publish a function version. For more information, see Improving startup performance with Lambda SnapStart .

ApplyOn.doc: When set to PublishedVersions , Lambda creates a snapshot of the execution environment when you publish a function version.

OptimizationStatus.doc: When you provide a qualified Amazon Resource Name (ARN) , this response element indicates whether SnapStart is activated for the specified function version.

RuntimeVersionConfig.doc: The ARN of the runtime and any errors that occured.

RuntimeVersionArn.doc: The ARN of the runtime version you want the function to use.

Error.doc: Error response when Lambda is unable to retrieve the runtime version for a function.

LoggingConfig.doc: The function's Amazon CloudWatch Logs configuration settings.

LogFormat.doc: The format in which Lambda sends your function's application and system logs to CloudWatch. Select between plain text and structured JSON.

ApplicationLogLevel.doc: Set this property to filter the application logs for your function that Lambda sends to CloudWatch. Lambda only sends application logs at the selected level of detail and lower, where TRACE is the highest level and FATAL is the lowest.

SystemLogLevel.doc: Set this property to filter the system logs for your function that Lambda sends to CloudWatch. Lambda only sends system logs at the selected level of detail and lower, where DEBUG is the highest level and WARN is the lowest.

LogGroup.doc: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch log group the function sends logs to. By default, Lambda functions send logs to a default log group named /aws/lambda/<function name> . To use a different log group, enter an existing log group or enter a new log group name.

lambda.ListLayers.doc: Lists Lambda layers and shows information about the latest version of each. Specify a runtime identifier to list only layers that indicate that they're compatible with that runtime. Specify a compatible architecture to include only layers that are compatible with that instruction set architecture .

NextMarker.doc: A pagination token returned when the response doesn't contain all layers.

LayerArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the function layer.

LatestMatchingVersion.doc: The newest version of the layer.

LayerVersionArn.doc: The ARN of the layer version.

CreatedDate.doc: The date that the version was created, in ISO 8601 format. For example, 2018-11-27T15:10:45.123+0000 .

CompatibleRuntimes.doc: The layer's compatible runtimes. The following list includes deprecated runtimes. For more information, see Runtime use after deprecation . For a list of all currently supported runtimes, see Supported runtimes .

CompatibleArchitectures.doc: A list of compatible instruction set architectures .

lambda.ListTags.doc: Returns a function, event source mapping, or code signing configuration's tags . You can also view function tags with GetFunction .
